title: Create Binary Tree From Descriptions
statement: Every entry of `descriptions` is a triple `[parent, child, isLeft]` saying that the node holding the value `child` hangs directly below the node holding the value `parent`: as its left child when `isLeft` is `1`, and as its right child when `isLeft` is `0`. Together the triples list every parent-to-child link of one binary tree in which no two nodes share a value, and they are guaranteed to describe a valid tree. Rebuild that tree and return its root.
constraints: The descriptions form one valid binary tree with distinct values
notes:
## Intuition

Each triple is one link of the tree, but the links arrive in no useful order: a child may be described before its parent is. If every value maps to a single node object, each triple can be applied the moment it is read, no matter when the other ends show up. The root is then the only value that never appears as a child. A brute force could search the whole list for each node's children, which costs O(n²).

## Approach

1. Keep `nodes`, a map from value to its `TreeNode`, and `children`, the set of values that hang below something.
2. `getNode(value)` returns the node for `value`, creating it the first time the value is seen.
3. For each `[parent, child, isLeft]`, look up both nodes and attach `childNode` to the left or right of `parentNode`. Record `child` in `children`.
4. Scan the parents again: the first one that is not in `children` is the root; return its node.

## Example 1, step by step

`descriptions = [[20,15,1],[20,17,0],[50,20,1],[50,80,0],[80,19,1]]`.

- `[20,15,1]` creates 20 and 15 and sets 15 as the left child of 20; `children = {15}`.
- `[20,17,0]` creates 17 as the right child of 20; `children = {15, 17}`.
- `[50,20,1]` creates 50 and reuses the existing 20 as its left child, so 20 keeps its own children.
- `[50,80,0]` and `[80,19,1]` add 80 to the right of 50 and 19 to the left of 80; `children = {15, 17, 20, 80, 19}`.
- The second pass skips 20 (twice) and stops at 50, which is never a child. In level order the tree is `[50,20,80,15,17,19]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) for n triples: each one costs a constant number of map and set operations.
- Space: O(n) for the map of nodes and the set of children.

## Pitfalls

- Create each value's node exactly once; making a fresh node for the same value twice splits the tree into pieces.
- Do not assume the first triple's parent is the root: the root may appear only in the last triple.
- Only parents can be the root, so searching the parent column is enough; a leaf never appears there.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nodes` | map from a value to its tree node |
| `children` | values that are some node's child |
| `getNode` | returns (creating if needed) the node for a value |
| `parent`, `child`, `isLeft` | the fields of the current triple |
| `parentNode`, `childNode` | the nodes for `parent` and `child` |
